news_drafts.headline: Carmarthenshire forecasts an £11.3m overspend for 2026/27, with £5.4m in Children's Services
news_drafts.lead:
Carmarthenshire County Council forecasts an overspend of £11.3m on its net revenue budget for 2026/27, according to the budget monitoring report before its Corporate Performance and Resources Scrutiny Committee. Across departments, including school budgets, the forecast overspend is £15.9m. The report says forecast departmental overspends are met from departmental reserves where available, and it gives no reserve balances.

Children's Services is forecast to overspend by a further £5.4m this year, after £12m of pressures funding allocated in previous years. The paper attributes this mainly to growth in the number of children in very high-cost residential placements, both in-house and commissioned. It reports more than 10 new placements since January 2026, partly offset by children turning 18 and moving to Adult Services. Schools are forecast to overspend their in-year budgets by £6.9m, which the paper acknowledges is an improvement on the same position a year earlier. It calls the trajectory "unsustainable" and says an intervention board will provide additional support.

For 2025/26, the council's net position was an overspend of £1.755m, transferred from general balances. Schools overspent by £7.7m, £5.3m of it in secondary schools, and school balances stood at a £9.6m deficit on 31 March 2026. Children's Services ended that year £3.6m over budget, £0.6m better than at the previous reporting period. The Welsh Government's employers' National Insurance grant came in just below £6.0m against a £7.0m budget assumption, and the £1.0m shortfall is built into the 2026/27 final budget.

news_drafts.headline: Carmarthenshire's Council Fund overspend reaches £1.76m, covered by reserve draw
news_drafts.lead: Carmarthenshire Council spent £1.755m more than its original budget in the year to 31 March 2026, and covered the shortfall by drawing from its general reserves. The Council Fund — the main account for day-to-day running costs — finished the year with General Balances of £15.497m. The council's Governance & Audit Committee received the outturn figures on 28 September. The overspend required a transfer from the reserve cushion the council holds for unexpected costs. Councils must hold sufficient reserves to manage in-year pressures and to smooth funding across years; the remaining balance provides the buffer for future risk.

news_drafts.headline: Dyfed Pension Fund cleared by auditors as investment income falls short by £6m
news_drafts.lead: Audit Wales has completed its 2025–26 audit of the Dyfed Pension Fund with no issues raised, giving the fund a clean financial bill of health. However, the fund is forecast to end the year £2.9m in deficit, driven chiefly by investment income falling £6m short of the amount budgeted. The fund was counting on that income to balance its books after employer contributions were cut following the 2025 actuarial valuation. The shortfall reflects lower distributions from fund managers and interest on cash holdings than anticipated. The fund has responded by building cash reserves to £18.5m — higher than historically held — described as a prudent measure given the structural changes to contributions.

findings.headline: Temporary Accommodation is forecast at £311k above working budget, offset in part by a £365k underspend in Homelessness.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the Temporary Accommodation overspend to bonds and prevention payments, which sit within Homelessness. Council Fund Housing overall is forecast at £583k above working budget.
findings.matters: Temporary accommodation costs are a demand-led pressure for housing authorities, and the reallocation between two lines shows how the forecast is being managed within the department.
findings.figures: £311k Temporary Accommodation variance; £365k Homelessness underspend; £583k Council Fund Housing variance
findings.quote: Overspend on Temporary Accommodation offset by underspend in Homelessness for bonds/prevention payments

findings.headline: Housing Benefits Admin is forecast at £62k above working budget, after a £253k shortfall on grant income against budget.
findings.detail: The paper records a net shortfall on grant income of £253k compared with budget. This is partly offset by nine current vacant posts, three of which are not expected to be filled this financial year, along with an anticipated underspend on supplies and services.
findings.matters: Administration grant shortfalls on benefits work are a recurring issue that other councils will want to compare against their own grant assumptions.
findings.figures: £253k grant income shortfall; £62k variance; nine current vacant posts
findings.quote: Net shortfall on grant income receivable of £253k compared with budget

findings.headline: Asylum Seekers & Resettlement schemes is forecast at £650k above working budget, because eligible resettlement expenditure is below the level budgeted.
findings.detail: The paper says the level of eligible expenditure relating to resettlement schemes will be significantly less than budgeted. Expenditure and income are both forecast at £775k, leaving a net variance of £650k.
findings.matters: Grant-funded resettlement income that depends on eligible spend can change quickly, and other councils running similar schemes will want to see how the eligibility shortfall is being reflected in their own forecasts.
findings.figures: £650k variance; £775k forecast expenditure; £775k forecast income; £650k budgeted income
findings.quote: The level of eligible expenditure within the department relating to the resettlement schemes will be significantly less than budgeted.

findings.headline: Council Tax Reduction Scheme is forecast at £224k above working budget because demand for the scheme has risen significantly.
findings.detail: The paper gives the forecast cost of the Council Tax Reduction Scheme as £22,801k against a working budget of £22,577k. It attributes the variance to a significant increase in demand for the scheme.
findings.matters: Demand-led council tax support costs are a direct charge on the council's collection base and are rising in many areas, so peers will compare their own scheme costs against this figure.
findings.quote: Council Tax Reduction Scheme 22,577 0 22,801 0 224 Significant increase in demand for the scheme

findings.headline: Miscellaneous Services is forecast at £295k below working budget, including a £243k underspend on pre-LGR pension costs.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the largest part of the Miscellaneous Services underspend to pre-LGR pension costs and a further £42k underspend on subscriptions. Together with other variances, the Financial Services division is forecast at £179k below budget.
findings.matters: Pre-reorganisation pension costs are a legacy liability for councils formed through local government reorganisation, and a finance director elsewhere will want to know how these costs are running against budget.
findings.figures: £295k Miscellaneous Services variance; £243k underspend on pre-LGR pension costs; £42k underspend on subscriptions
findings.quote: £243k underspend on pre LGR pension costs
